detail:
NIDDK describes interstitial cystitis (IC), also called bladder pain syndrome, as a chronic, or long-lasting, condition that causes painful urinary symptoms. The institute estimates that between 4 and 12 million people in the United States may have IC, and notes that the exact number is uncertain because IC can be mistaken for other conditions. The cause is not established in the sources.

NIDDK notes that symptoms can include discomfort, pressure, tenderness, or pain in the bladder, lower abdomen, and pelvic area, along with urinary urgency and frequency. Sources describe diagnosis as a process of ruling out other conditions with similar symptoms, using medical history, a physical exam, and laboratory and other tests, rather than a single definitive test.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about interstitial cystitis symptoms and diagnosis.
sourceName: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

symptoms can include bladder and pelvic pain, urgency, and frequency
diagnosis works by ruling out other conditions with similar symptoms
title: Interstitial Cystitis / Bladder Pain Syndrome: chronic bladder pain with no single test
